original_question: Between GM1 gangliosidoses and lysosomal storage diseases as a group, which condition has a lower incidence based on their respective prevalence ranges?

final_qi.question: What is the prevalence range of GM1 gangliosidoses?
final_qi.long_answer: GM1 gangliosidosis is an ultra-rare lysosomal storage disorder caused by GLB1 deficiency; epidemiologic surveys and registry data place its birth prevalence at roughly one affected individual per 100,000 to 200,000 live births worldwide.

final_qi.question: What is the prevalence range of lysosomal storage diseases as a group?
final_qi.long_answer: Collectively, lysosomal storage diseases are rare but, as a group, they occur in roughly one out of every 5,000 to 8,000 live births worldwide. This aggregate prevalence is derived from population-based newborn screening and epidemiological studies that pool the frequencies of the more than 50 individual lysosomal disorders.
